column2: Rainwater slowly soaks into the soil and becomes groundwater, which many towns pump up for drinking.
column3: 雨水慢慢滲入土壤成為地下水，許多城鎮把它抽上來飲用。
column5: ground 地面 + water 水：藏在地面下的水

column2: Sandy soil is highly permeable, so rainwater drains through it quickly instead of forming puddles.
column3: 沙質土壤非常容易透水，所以雨水很快排掉，而不會形成水坑。
column5: per 穿過 + meable 走：水能一路穿過去

column2: Clay is nearly impermeable, which is why ponds lined with it can hold water for months.
column3: 黏土幾乎不透水，所以鋪了黏土的池塘能把水留住好幾個月。
column5: im 不 + permeable 可滲透：水穿不過去

column2: Percolation through layers of sand and gravel removes dirt, giving the city clean drinking water.
column3: 水穿過沙層與礫石層的滲濾作用能去除髒汙，為城市提供乾淨的飲用水。
column5: per 穿過 + colate 過濾：像咖啡濾杯慢慢滴下去

column2: The seismic waves from the earthquake traveled through the planet and were recorded on the other side of the world.
column3: 地震的震波穿過地球，在世界另一端被記錄下來。
column5: seismic 像「賽絲米克」：賽，絲絲震動就知道

column2: A seismograph in the basement drew a jagged line on paper whenever the ground shook.
column3: 地下室裡的地震儀每當地面晃動，就在紙上畫出鋸齒狀的線。
column5: seismo 地震 + graph 畫：把地震畫成線的儀器

column2: The epicenter of the quake was located ten kilometers beneath a small farming town.
column3: 這次地震的震央位在一個小農鎮地下十公里處。
column4: the epicenter of the quake (地震的震央)
column5: epi 在上 + center 中心：正好在震源上方的中心

column2: The San Andreas fault runs for hundreds of kilometers, and the rocks on either side slowly slide past each other.
column3: 聖安地列斯斷層綿延數百公里，兩側的岩石緩慢地相互滑動。
column4: along a fault line (沿著斷層線)
column5: fault 與 fall 相近：地層裂開，一邊往下掉

column2: After the earthquake, a long fissure opened in the road, and steam began to rise from it.
column3: 地震之後，路面裂開一道長長的縫，蒸氣開始從中冒出。
column5: fiss 裂開：像把魚刀切開（fish 發音）的長縫

column2: Scientists consider the volcano dormant because it has not erupted in two hundred years, but it could wake up.
column3: 科學家認為這座火山處於休眠狀態，因為它兩百年來未噴發，但仍可能甦醒。
column5: dorm 睡覺（dormitory 宿舍）：火山正在睡覺

column2: Unlike an active volcano, an extinct volcano will never erupt again because its magma supply has disappeared.
column3: 與活火山不同，死火山永遠不會再噴發，因為它的岩漿來源已消失。
column5: ex 出 + tinct 熄：火焰熄滅，不再活動

column2: Every ninety minutes, the geyser shoots boiling water thirty meters into the air, delighting tourists.
column3: 這座間歇泉每九十分鐘就把沸水噴向三十公尺高空，讓遊客非常開心。
column4: an erupting geyser (噴發的間歇泉)
column5: geyser 像「蓋噎舍」：蓋子噎住，一下噴出水柱

column2: A stalactite hangs from the cave ceiling like an icicle, formed drop by drop from dissolved minerals.
column3: 鐘乳石像冰柱一樣從洞頂垂下，由溶解的礦物一滴一滴形成。
column5: c 是 ceiling 天花板：tite 緊緊（tight）掛在頂上

column2: Beneath each dripping stalactite, a stalagmite slowly grows upward from the cave floor.
column3: 每一根滴水的鐘乳石下方，都有石筍從洞底緩緩向上生長。
column4: stalagmite grows upward (石筍向上生長)
column5: g 是 ground 地面：mite 從地面往上爬

column2: Few trees can grow in the tundra, where the ground stays frozen and winters last most of the year.
column3: 苔原上幾乎長不出樹，因為地面一直結凍，冬天占了一年的大部分時間。
column5: tundra 像「吞的拉」：凍得讓人吞口水的荒原

column2: As permafrost thaws in Siberia, it releases gases that were trapped in the frozen ground for thousands of years.
column3: 隨著西伯利亞的永凍層融化，它釋放出被困在冰凍土中數千年的氣體。
column5: perma 永久（permanent）+ frost 霜：永遠不化的霜

column2: Scientists found strange shrimp living near hydrothermal vents, where hot water gushes out of the ocean floor.
column3: 科學家發現奇特的蝦子住在熱液噴口附近，那裡的熱水從海底湧出。
column5: hydro 水 + thermal 熱：熱水

column2: Birds may use the geomagnetic field to navigate, sensing Earth's magnetism the way a compass does.
column3: 鳥類可能利用地磁場來導航，像指南針一樣感測地球的磁性。
column5: geo 地球 + magnetic 磁性：地球像一塊大磁鐵

column2: Earth's atmosphere contains about twenty-one percent oxygen, which makes life possible on the surface.
column3: 地球的大氣層含有約百分之二十一的氧氣，使地表生命得以存在。
column5: atmo 蒸氣 + sphere 球：包著地球的氣體球

column2: The crust under the oceans is thinner than the crust under the continents, averaging only seven kilometers.
column3: 海洋下方的地殼比大陸下方的薄，平均只有七公里。
column5: crust 是麵包硬皮：地球最外面那層硬殼

column2: Heat in the mantle causes slow, churning currents that push the plates of the crust across the planet.
column3: 地函中的熱量引起緩慢的翻攪流動，推動地殼板塊在地球上移動。
column5: mantle 是披風：披在地核外面的厚厚一層

column2: Earth's core, made mostly of iron and nickel, is almost as hot as the surface of the sun.
column3: 地球的地核主要由鐵與鎳組成，溫度幾乎和太陽表面一樣高。
column5: core 是蘋果芯：地球最裡面的核心

column2: Alfred Wegener proposed continental drift after noticing that the coasts of Africa and South America seemed to fit together.
column3: 魏格納注意到非洲與南美洲的海岸線似乎能拼合，因而提出大陸漂移學說。
column4: the theory of continental drift (大陸漂移說)
column5: continent 大陸 + drift 漂流：大陸像船一樣慢慢漂

column2: Plate tectonics explains why mountains rise, volcanoes erupt, and earthquakes occur along the edges of moving slabs of rock.
column3: 板塊構造學說解釋了為何山脈隆起、火山噴發，以及地震發生在移動岩板的邊緣。
column4: theory of plate tectonics (板塊構造學說)
column5: plate 盤子 + tectonics 構造：地殼像一塊塊盤子在移動

column2: At the Japan Trench, the Pacific Plate sinks beneath another plate in a process called subduction.
column3: 在日本海溝，太平洋板塊沉入另一塊板塊下方，此過程稱為隱沒作用。
column5: sub 下面 + duct 引導：被引到下面去

column2: Where the river meets the sea, it drops its sand and mud and builds a fertile delta.
column3: 河流入海處會沉積沙泥，形成肥沃的三角洲。
column5: delta 是希臘字母 Δ：三角形的河口

column2: The Missouri is a major tributary of the Mississippi, adding huge amounts of water as it joins the main river.
column3: 密蘇里河是密西西比河的一條主要支流，匯入幹流時帶來大量的水。
column4: a tributary of the river (河的支流)
column5: tribute 進貢：小河向大河進貢河水

column2: Farmers prize the alluvial plains because floods deposit rich, dark soil there each spring.
column3: 農民珍視沖積平原，因為每年春天洪水都會在那裡留下肥沃的黑土。
column5: al 朝向 + luv 洗（lavatory 洗手間）：被水沖來的土

column2: After the flood receded, a thick layer of silt covered the fields and fertilized the soil.
column3: 洪水退去後，一層厚厚的淤泥覆蓋了田野，也使土壤更肥沃。
column5: silt 像「西爾特」：水退後沉下去的細軟泥

column2: Engineers drilled down to the bedrock before building the tower, so the foundations would not sink.
column3: 工程師在蓋塔前先鑽到基岩，讓地基不會下沉。
column5: bed 床 + rock 岩石：所有土層下面的那張石床

column2: The long ridge of boulders and gravel is a moraine, left behind when the glacier melted and retreated.
column3: 那道由巨石與礫石組成的長脊是冰磧，是冰河融化退去時留下的。
column5: moraine 像「摸壤」：冰河退去後摸到的碎石堆

column2: Cruise ships glide between steep cliffs in the Norwegian fjord, a deep inlet carved by an ancient glacier.
column3: 郵輪在挪威峽灣陡峭的懸崖間滑行，那是遠古冰河切出來的深海灣。
column5: fjord 像「飛喔」：船在峽灣中飛過，兩邊山壁高聳

column2: Indonesia is an archipelago of more than seventeen thousand islands scattered across warm tropical seas.
column3: 印尼是一個群島國家，有一萬七千多座島嶼散布在溫暖的熱帶海域。
column5: archi 主要 + pelago 海：以海為主體，島嶼散布其中

column2: Italy is a long peninsula, surrounded by sea on three sides and joined to Europe by land on the fourth.
column3: 義大利是一個狹長半島，三面環海，一面與歐洲相連。
column5: pen 幾乎 + insula 島：幾乎是島，只差一邊連陸

column2: The Isthmus of Panama is a narrow strip of land that links North and South America.
column3: 巴拿馬地峽是連結北美洲與南美洲的一條狹長陸地。
column5: isthmus 的 th 不發音 th：像「艾斯母斯」，兩邊是海夾著細腰

column2: Ships bound for the Black Sea must pass through the narrow Bosphorus strait near Istanbul.
column3: 前往黑海的船隻必須經過伊斯坦堡附近狹窄的博斯普魯斯海峽。
column4: strait of Gibraltar (直布羅陀海峽)
column5: strait 與 straight 近：兩塊陸地夾出一條直直的水路

column2: Few crops grow on the high plateau, where the air is thin and the winters are cold.
column3: 高原上很少作物能生長，因為那裡空氣稀薄，冬天又冷。
column5: plateau 像「破樓」：爬上破樓頂，平平的一片大平台

column2: Over millions of years, the Colorado River carved a vast canyon with walls over a mile high.
column3: 數百萬年來，科羅拉多河切出一道壁高逾一英里的巨大峽谷。
column5: canyon 像「肯楊」：肯定很深，楊起頭才看到頂

column2: Hikers crossed a narrow bridge over the gorge, where a river rushed far below between steep rock walls.
column3: 登山客走過峽谷上的窄橋，河水在陡峭岩壁之間於遠遠下方奔流。
column5: gorge 像「過去」：夾在高崖間一過去就是深谷

column2: Deep-sea cameras revealed strange fish living in the abyss, thousands of meters below the sunlit ocean surface.
column3: 深海攝影機拍到奇特的魚類生活在深淵中，位於陽光照得到的海面下數千公尺處。
column5: a 無 + byss 底：沒有底的地方
